name: Titanium dioxide
what_it_is: A bright white powder, the same pigment used in paint and sunscreen.
why_its_added: Makes food and coatings look opaque white, mostly in sweets and icings.

india.note: Permitted at GMP level - used as needed, no fixed numeric cap in the categories found.

eu.note: Banned in food in the EU since 2022. EFSA concluded in May 2021 that titanium dioxide can no longer be considered safe as a food additive, because a concern over genotoxicity could not be ruled out and no acceptable daily intake could be set.

usa.note: Listed colour additive, exempt from batch certification (21 CFR 73.575)

eu_safety_opinion.title: Safety assessment of titanium dioxide (E171) as a food additive

replaced_an_older_opinion.title: Re-evaluation of titanium dioxide -E 171- as a food additive

safe_daily_limit.no_number_means: EFSA has not set a number for this one. That can mean it is considered safe enough not to need a limit, or that the evidence was not sufficient to set one. The opinion itself says which.

means: No single-serving limit has been found for this substance. That is not the same as there being no risk from one large serving - it means nobody has published a number.

people_reports.rule: Reports are shown as reports. We count them. We never turn them into a health claim, and we never let them change the sourced facts above.

india_limits.food_category: Salt (including edible common salt, iron fortified salt, iodized salt)*
